story_type: Marine combat engineers demolition range: obstacles, charges, close-up blasts
hook: Marine engineers blew up a forty pound cratering charge.
narration: This is a Marine demolition range at Camp Lejeune, the moment the charges go off.
First the engineers built obstacles: tanglefoot, triple strand concertina wire and cattle fence.
Then they spent hours building the charges to clear them.
A cratering charge blows a deep hole in the ground, turning a road into a ditch no vehicle can cross.
They also used Claymores, TNT, dynamite and Bangalore torpedoes.
outcome: The charges went off and threw smoke and dirt across the range.
title: Marines set off a 40 lb cratering charge
description:
Marine combat engineers with Combat Logistics Battalion 22 set off Bangalore torpedoes, Claymore mines and a 40 pound cratering charge on a demolition range at Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, in 2017.

Footage: U.S. Marine Corps video by Sgt. Clemente Garcia, II Marine Expeditionary Force, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/514946/clb-22-shakes-things-up-with-demolition
